page.layout: One page of running text, with a bracketed synopsis in the middle of the text and a catchword at the lower right. Running head at top left and the page number with "Lib. 5." at top right. The right edge of the scan shows the cropped margin of the facing page, which is not transcribed.

main_text.head: Atq; hæc erga corpus.
main_text.p: Primum, vt ita apud omnes viuamus, vt nulla offensione data, vitæ sanctimonia, ipsos ad pietatem exemplo nostro incitemus. 1.Cor.10.32.
Secundum, vt omnes occasiones captemus, vt alios ad bonum perseq-uendum, ad mala abrumpenda lucrefcamus. 1.Cor.10.33.
main_text.head: Atq; hæ sunt speciales leges ad aliorum necessitates referendæ.
main_text.p: Ad mala referendæ sunt, vel quæ versantur
Ea autem est virtus qua summa solicitudine, verbis factisue, causas & occasiones offensionum, discordiarum & odiorum auertamus. Gene. 13.7.8.9.10.
Quare hic sæpius de iure nostro alijs cedendum. Ibid.
Huc etiam pertinent ea fœdera, quæ cum omnibus sanctè iniri possunt.
Ea autem sunt quæ de ijs officijs, quæ omnibus debentur, sancita fuerint. Gen.21.22.24.27.28.30. &c. Mal.2.10.

page.notes: The right edge shows cropped fragments of the facing page's margin notes (ti, ir, iu, p, li, fe, &, ve, me, 3.2, nat, 18., rat, tib, app, ciat, ber, cian). They belong to the neighbouring page and are not transcribed. The Greek word "φιλησυχία" in the text is read with doubt; the scan is small. The Greek word "Επιείκεια" is also set in italic type on the scan. The bracketed synopsis is given as lines of text.
